assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cytosine and adenine base editors turned genome editing into precise chemistry on a single nucleotide: engineered deaminase-Cas fusions that convert one base pair to another without double-strand breaks. It is rational molecular design that gave researchers and clinicians a new capability, and base-edited therapies are already in patients. Important, original and clear in its chemical logic.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the laboratory; Komor (cytosine base editor) and Gaudelli (adenine base editor, which required evolving a deaminase for DNA) made the decisive first-author contributions. The Nishida/Kondo cytidine-deaminase work (Target-AID) was independent and near-simultaneous, so a three-person prize would leave a priority question open.
assessment.maturity: Replicated widely and in clinical use since 2018 to 2020. Timing is good, though the 2020 CRISPR prize recognized the Cas9 platform and the committee may see this as a sequel.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2020 CRISPR prize and with the related prime editing candidate
Credit for Target-AID (Nishida, Kondo) versus the Liu-lab editors
Long-term clinical safety and efficacy are still emerging

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation hijacks E3 ligases with bifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues, making previously undruggable proteins tractable. It is a new chemical modality, and the thalidomide/cereblon mechanism turns an old drug story into a design principle. Strong clinical translation, with degraders in late-stage trials.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies introduced the PROTAC concept (2001); Handa and Ito identified cereblon as the thalidomide target; Ciulli, Gray and others advanced VHL ligands and degrader chemistry. The field has several parallel lines, so a clean three-way split is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is well confirmed and many degraders are in clinical trials, but no approved PROTAC drug yet, so clinical validation is still maturing.
uncertainties: Whether PROTACs and molecular glues should be recognized together
No approved PROTAC yet
Choice between Handa and Ito or Ciulli for the glue/E3 ligand component

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation reframed how cells organize biochemistry without membranes, linking physical chemistry of polymers to cell biology, disease and condensate-targeted drug discovery. Highly influential and conceptually original.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman (P granules, 2009) are the founding experimental pair; Rosen (multivalent signaling-protein phase separation, 2012) is a third, independent foundation. Pappu and Mittag contribute sequence-grammar theory, which makes a three-person limit hard.
assessment.maturity: Very broad uptake, but debate continues on physiological relevance in cells and on the rigor of in vitro versus in vivo evidence. Possibly slightly early.
uncertainties: Whether many reported condensates are functionally relevant in vivo
Credit for sequence-encoded theory (Pappu, Mittag)
Fit with Chemistry versus Medicine or Physiology

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the enabling chemistry for siRNA and mRNA medicines (patisiran, COVID-19 vaccines). Delivery of nucleic acids is a nanomaterials and bioengineering problem of exactly the kind where chemistry changed what clinicians can do.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and collaborators developed the ionizable lipid and rapid-mixing formulation concept; Anderson and Langer contributed combinatorial lipidoid discovery. Several industrial and academic contributors (MacLachlan, Hope, Madden) make selection contentious. My three names are a judgment, not a settled attribution.
assessment.maturity: Validated by billions of vaccine doses and approved siRNA drugs. Mature impact, though the 2023 Medicine prize already honored mRNA modification, so timing relative to that is delicate.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize on mRNA vaccines
Distribution of credit among academic and company inventors
Patent and priority disputes may cloud attribution

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs allow site-specific incorporation of noncanonical amino acids in living cells, giving programmable chemistry of proteins. A broadly used tool in biophysics, biotherapeutics and chemical biology, with a clear conceptual advance.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang established the first in vivo incorporation in E. coli and eukaryotes; Chin extended the code to multiple codons, quadruplet decoding and synthetic organisms. Yokoyama and Mehl are real contributors but less central.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of independent confirmation and widespread use. Fully mature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether a prize would favor the foundational Schultz work or later Chin advances
Schultz's profile and field politics may affect committee appetite

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA-programmed assembly of nanoparticles and spherical nucleic acids gave programmable recognition on a nanoparticle surface, underpinning colorimetric diagnostics, intracellular gene regulation and crystal engineering. This is close to my own field of peptide- or DNA-gold hybrids and bioanalytical readouts; I judge it highly original.
assessment.attribution: Mirkin's lab produced the key 1996 DNA-gold assembly and the spherical nucleic acid concept; Alivisatos published a contemporaneous DNA-nanocrystal work. Storhoff and Mucic were trainees on the Mirkin papers. Mirkin alone or with Alivisatos is the most defensible configuration.
assessment.maturity: Decades of follow-up, commercial diagnostics and some clinical trials, but clinical impact is less established than for other medical candidates.
uncertainties: Relative contribution of Alivisatos versus Mirkin
Limited clinical translation to date
Competition from the quantum-dot prize of 2023 for nanochemistry slots

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Shokat's chemical genetics of kinases and covalent targeting of the KRAS G12C mutant cysteine overturned the idea that KRAS was undruggable and led to sotorasib and adagrasib. A clean example of chemistry transforming oncology.
assessment.attribution: A single credited person, which gives a simple and defensible configuration; downstream drug development involved industrial teams, but the discovery of the switch-II pocket tethering strategy is Shokat's.
assessment.maturity: Approved drugs since 2021 with several years of clinical data; resistance mechanisms are a remaining issue, but the discovery itself is mature.
uncertainties: A single-person prize may be thought too narrow for the broader KRAS and kinase story
Contribution of the Ostrem/Shokat 2013 paper versus industrial optimization

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Sequencing-by-synthesis with reversible terminators (Solexa/Illumina) is the chemical engine of massively parallel sequencing, one of the most consequential analytical technologies in biomedicine. Chemistry and single-molecule detection are central.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman founded the Solexa approach and carried it to practice; Rothberg (454) and Ju (terminator chemistry) are also credited with technology contributions, and Mayer a further route. The competing lines make attribution complicated.
assessment.maturity: Entirely mature, with transformative impact for two decades. If anything, it is long overdue, though debates over which method deserves the credit persist.
uncertainties: Competing sequencing technologies and priority disputes
Whether committee considers it chemistry or biology/medicine
